title: Regular generation of a flat quotient ideal detected on the closed fibre
statement: Let $a:(A,\mathfrak m)\to(T,\mathfrak n)$ be a flat local homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] of Noetherian local commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means $a(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Let $K\subseteq\mathfrak n$ be an ideal and assume $T/K$ is flat over $A$. Put $\overline T=T/\mathfrak mT$ and $\overline K=(K+\mathfrak mT)/\mathfrak mT$, an ideal of $\overline T$. Then $K$ is generated by a finite $T$-regular sequence if and only if $\overline K$ is generated by a finite $\overline T$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Empty sequences are allowed; no finite-type or finite-presentation hypothesis on $A\to T$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CEP (lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra), base change of regular equations with flat quotient, using Noetherian local equivalence of regular and quasi-regular sequences; converse from algebra.tex Tag 00MG (lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence) and Nakayama, after flatness identifies K/(mK) with its closed-fibre image.

proof.text: Put $k=A/\mathfrak m$ and $I=\mathfrak mT$. Locality gives $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Thus $\overline T=T/I$ is a nonzero local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n/I$: maximal ideals of the quotient correspond to maximal ideals of $T$ containing $I$. It is Noetherian, since the preimage of any ideal is finitely generated in $T$ and the images of those generators generate the quotient ideal. Also $\overline K\subseteq\mathfrak n/I$ is proper.

source.place: Noetherian quotient and local quotient arguments from definitions; preparation for Tag 00MG (lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence).

proof.text: First suppose $K=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ with $(f_i)$ $T$-regular. The regular-sequence graded-polynomial lemma gives the canonical isomorphism $(T/K)[X_1,\ldots,X_r]\cong\operatorname{gr}_K(T)$. Apply quasi-regular flat-quotient base change to $A\to T$, $A\to k$, using the assumed $A$-flatness of $T/K$. Identify $T\otimes_A k$ with $T/I=\overline T$ by the quotient base-change lemma, which sends $f_i\otimes1$ to $\overline f_i$. Their ideal is $\overline K$, and the canonical graded-polynomial map for this list is an isomorphism. Since $\overline T$ is Noetherian local and every $\overline f_i$ lies in its maximal ideal, quasi-regularity implies regularity by the cited Noetherian-local lemma. This proves the forward implication without a finite-presentation hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0CEP (lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra), part (1), combined with algebra.tex Tags 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), 061S (lemma-quasi-regular-regular), and 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact).

proof.text: For the converse, tensor $0\to K\to T\to T/K\to0$ over $A$ with $k$. The flat-quotient tensor-injectivity lemma applies because $T/K$ is $A$-flat; it gives an injection $k\otimes_AK\to k\otimes_AT$. By the quotient-module tensor formula these modules identify with $K/\mathfrak mK$ and $T/\mathfrak mT$, and the map sends $x\bmod\mathfrak mK$ to $x\bmod\mathfrak mT$. Its image is exactly $\overline K$. Consequently $K\cap\mathfrak mT=\mathfrak mK$ and $K/\mathfrak mK\cong\overline K$, as $\overline T$-modules. Here $\mathfrak mK=(\mathfrak mT)K=IK$, since expanding a generator $a(u)t$ with $u\in\mathfrak m$ gives $a(u)(tx)$.

source.place: Tags 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero) and 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact), applied to the ideal sequence and reduction modulo the maximal ideal.

proof.text: Choose a finite regular generating list $\overline f_1,\ldots,\overline f_r$ of $\overline K$, and lift each element to $f_i\in K$. Put $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq K$. The isomorphism of step 3 gives $K=J+IK$: for $x\in K$, express its image using the $\overline f_i$, lift the coefficients to $T$, and subtract that combination; the difference lies in $IK$. The $T$-module $M=K/J$ is finite because $T$ is Noetherian. Thus $IM=M$. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak n=\operatorname{rad}(T)$, Nakayama gives $M=0$, so $J=K$.

source.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (2), applied to K/J and the ideal mT.

proof.text: Apply the Grothendieck closed-fibre lifting lemma to the original flat local map $A\to T$ of Noetherian local rings and the chosen list $f_1,\ldots,f_r$. Its images are the given regular list in $T/\mathfrak mT$, so the lifted list is $T$-regular. Together with $J=K$ this proves the reverse implication. For $r=0$, the same Nakayama argument gives $K=0$ when $\overline K=0$; the empty list is regular in both nonzero local rings. In the forward direction the graded-polynomial and base-change statements also allow the empty list.

source.place: Tag 00MG (lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence), including the empty-list case, and Tag 00LF (definition-regular-sequence).
